Yaruha Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Yaruha's Jewish community specialized in wine making from its earliest years, later diversifying into tobacco cultivation; the population actually grew between 1897 and 1926, from 1,271 to 1,833, despite the intervening turmoil of WWI and the Civil War. A hospital and free canteen were organized within the wartime ghetto here in spring 1942, even as many residents were murdered locally or deported to share the fate of the Jews in Mohyliv-Podilskyi, documented elsewhere in this collection. This is the older of Yaruha's two Jewish cemeteries, established in the early 19th century, with its last burial in 1940.
